introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL TWO questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first 2 will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Na = 23.0, Cu = 64.0, Cl = 35.5, K = 39.0, N = 14.0, S = 32.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown: A current of 2.5 amperes was passed through a solution of the salt of an element, X, for one hour. (X is not the usual symbol of the element). The element X was deposited at the cathode.
incertitudes: Section A : l'en-tête dit « ANSWER ALL 5 questions. You will be graded for the best 4 answers ». La règle structurée « 4 sur 5 » traduit la notation sur les 4 meilleures réponses ; l'élève doit tout de même traiter les 5 (le texte exact figure dans l'introduction).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State whether X is a metal or a non metal.

(ii) Give a reason for your answer. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) X is a **metal**.

(ii) X was deposited at the **cathode**, the negative electrode. Only positive ions (cations) move to the cathode, and metals form positive ions; non-metals form negative ions (except hydrogen) which go to the anode.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate:

(i) The quantity of electricity in coulombs used in the experiment.

(ii) The number of Faradays of electricity used during the experiment. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Quantity of electricity $Q = I \times t$, with $t = 1\ \text{hour} = 3600\ \mathrm{s}$:

$Q = 2.5 \times 3600 = 9000\ \mathrm{C}$

(ii) $1\ \text{faraday} = 96000\ \mathrm{C}$, so

$\text{number of faradays} = \dfrac{9000}{96000} = 0.09375 \approx 0.094\ \mathrm{F}$

questions.enonce_markdown: If 10.8 g of X were collected during the experiment, calculate the number of moles of X collected (RMM of X = 108). *[2 marks]*
Electrolysis is used to electroplate articles. Draw a diagram to show the set up you would use to electroplate an iron spoon with silver indicating clearly the electrodes and electrolyte. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Diagram to draw:** a beaker (electrolytic cell) containing the electrolyte, with two electrodes dipping into it and connected to a d.c. source (battery) through a switch.

- **Electrolyte:** a solution of a silver salt, e.g. aqueous **silver nitrate**, $\mathrm{AgNO_3(aq)}$.
- **Cathode (negative electrode):** the **iron spoon** (the article to be plated), connected to the negative terminal of the battery.
- **Anode (positive electrode):** a bar of **pure silver**, connected to the positive terminal.

Reactions: at the cathode $\mathrm{Ag^+} + \mathrm{e^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ag}$ (a layer of silver is deposited on the spoon); at the anode $\mathrm{Ag} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ag^+} + \mathrm{e^-}$, so the concentration of the electrolyte stays constant.
